source.title: Interpreting Video Representations with Spatio-Temporal Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether SAE features are monosemantic and temporally stable in video encoders. It finds temporal instability in standard SAEs and shows that monosemanticity scores depend substantially on the similarity space, refining the claim that SAE features are stable, canonical units. It does not test superposition geometry or toy networks.
record.gate_note: Relevant results concern SAE feature monosemanticity scores, temporal coherence, and targeted ablation of features. The paper also reports probe accuracy, action purity, reconstruction, and retrieval, but most of those results do not directly establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units; those unrelated results are not cataloged here. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study applies TopK SAEs to frozen video encoders (DINOv2, VideoMAE) and mainly reports how its own contrastive and Matryoshka SAE variants perform. Its measures do not bear on any version. Lag-1 autocorrelation is frame-to-frame activation consistency, not whether the dictionary is stable or canonical across training. MonoSemanticity (MS) scores and the backbone-alignment artifact are about an evaluation metric, not completeness or canonicality. Probe-weight ablations show what a linear probe relies on. The subjects are vision encoders, not LLMs, so V4 is not tested, and there are no toy models, neuron polysemanticity or multi-dimensional feature tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors trace the incoherence to hard TopK selection and that contrastive and Matryoshka objectives recover or exceed raw coherence. They also report that contrastive SAE features improve action probing (+3.9 pp) and text-video retrieval (up to 2.8× R@1). They stress that no variant dominates every goal.
record.recipe_differences: This is an application of TopK SAEs and added spatio-temporal contrastive or Matryoshka objectives to video vision encoders, not a reproduction of the toy-network feature-superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: MonoSemanticity scores depend on the choice of similarity backbone. Temporal coherence changes with SAE variant and contrastive setting; the paper also reports layer-dependent severity and says benefits differ between DINOv2 and VideoMAE.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard TopK SAE activations on DINOv2 video features lose temporal coherence: lag-1 falls from 0.435 (raw) to 0.277, with 95% of features below 0.3. Contrastive training can restore it (0.462).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature activations are temporally consistent across video frames when the underlying content is stable.

fits_no_version.finding: Own-space MS differs about 2.7× between backbones (0.97 vs 0.32–0.37). Under CLIP similarity, all entries converge to 0.67–0.68.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE monosemanticity scores are comparable across models independent of the similarity space used.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing the top probe-weighted SAE features drops action-probe accuracy sharply (Temporal: 20.2% to 10.9% at N=10). Zeroing the same number of random features barely changes it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-relevant information in SAE dictionaries is concentrated in a few identifiable features.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’26), as stated in the paper.
record.problems: The feature-unit evidence is task- and metric-dependent: MonoSemanticity scores vary with similarity space, temporal coherence varies by variant, and targeted ablation measures importance to a linear action probe rather than completeness or canonicality. The paper reports 3 seeds but does not give uncertainty values for these MonoSemanticity or coherence table entries.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were kept for the paper's other probe, action-purity, reconstruction, retrieval, or soft-sparsity results because they do not directly measure whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical representation units. Table 3 targeted ablation rows not described in the text were also omitted; the selected rows capture the stated standard, temporal, raster, and Separate+M findings and their corresponding random controls.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity–dimension transition, or geometry analysis.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
Vision encoders only; no LLMs, and no measure of features spread across neurons.
No completeness, cross-seed or cross-size stability, or canonicality test of the dictionaries.
No comparison of 1-D against multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' judgement for V5 relies on reading 'stable' as temporal coherence of activations, which is a different construct. All rows are relinked to none. A frozen random-decoder control (R² 0.910 learned vs 0.578 frozen, similar probe accuracy) is also reported but is not recorded as a row.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy networks, feature sparsity versus dimensionality, overlap geometry, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
The study does not test neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of limited capacity, or competition between important and less-important features.
The study does not test polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of neuron polysemanticity.
The subjects are video vision encoders, not LLMs. The study does not measure feature distribution across LLM neurons.
It tests SAE feature monosemanticity scores and temporal consistency in video representations, but not whether the dictionary is complete, canonical, or uniquely determined.
The study uses sparse latents but does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Standard TopK SAE features on DINOv2/SSv2
reader_labels.reason: Temporal coherence falls from raw lag-1 0.435 to 0.277, with 95% of features below 0.3; the paper describes flickering activations (r25–r26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MonoSemanticity scores across backbones and similarity spaces
reader_labels.reason: Own-space scores differ strongly between DINOv2 and VideoMAE, while CLIP-space scores converge around 0.67–0.68; the authors identify a backbone-alignment artifact (r1–r24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Learned temporal and spatio-temporal variants on DINOv2/SSv2
reader_labels.reason: Some learned variants partially recover temporal coherence, and Temporal+M at τ=0.2 exceeds the raw reference, but results vary by variant and setting (r27–r32).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Ablations show that identifiable features can carry predictive signal, but this task-specific probe evidence does not establish complete or canonical representation units (r36–r43).
